description: Per-agent model routing. Telegram chat uses telegram_model; inbox/work tasks use inbox_model; if a call fails, fallback_model is tried. Pinned explicitly to model IDs to avoid alias ambiguity.

beacon.name: Beacon
beacon.note: Opus everywhere — spec authoring is judgment-heavy and the spec is the contract. Don't economize. PILOT 2026-05-30: first agent on claude-opus-4-8 (see _history). fallback stays sonnet for graceful degradation.

forge.name: Forge
forge.note: Sonnet for chat / routine implementation. Opus for hard tasks (architecture, debugging, security review). Forge can self-escalate to Opus mid-task by setting model in the inbox handshake. worktree_enabled: dispatches go into /tmp/wt-forge-<task_id>/ via worktree_manager; allowed_repos gates target_repo on inbox writes.

mirror.name: Mirror
mirror.note: Opus for actual reviews. Sonnet acceptable for chat / status queries. worktree_enabled: review dispatches go into a per-task worktree (~/agent-worktrees/wt-mirror-<task_id>/) so Mirror can gh pr checkout the branch and run tests against the PR. allowed_repos gates target_repo on inbox writes (same shape as Forge). review_slots=2 (mirror-two-slot-review-spec §4 PR3): spawns two concurrent review watcher threads consuming the one mirror inbox; the slot plumbing landed inert in PR1/PR2. Rollback = set to 1 (or delete the key) + restart the watcher (spec §6.4).

pulse.name: Pulse
pulse.note: Sonnet for routine cycles (cheap polling). Pulse can self-escalate to Opus when investigating a recurring pattern. Default cycle frequency starts at 30 min; tune as we earn trust.

aide.name: Aide
aide.note: EA tasks are mostly mechanical (drafting emails, scheduling, calendar holds). Sonnet handles them well. Opus reserved for ambiguous prioritization calls.

scout.name: Scout
scout.note: Sonnet for chat / Q&A. Opus for actual deep research (competitive analysis, technical deep-dives). Scout's output quality matters — research that misleads is worse than no research.

compass.name: Compass
compass.note: Sequencing across multiple in-flight projects is judgment work. Opus default.

loop_bounds._note: D3.5 loop budgets. max_revisions caps Forge↔Mirror revision cycles (5b). max_replans caps Beacon↔Larry replan cycles after Mirror ESCALATE (5c). cost_per_task_usd is the per-task_id spend cap across all dispatches (preflight + clarifications + build + revisions + reviews + replans). Read by outbox_notifier when classifying Mirror markers. mirror_marker_self_validate_retries (mirror-marker-self-validate-gate-001) caps the SAME-PROCESS verdict-marker self-validation re-prompt loop in inbox_watcher.process_task: when a phase=review Mirror output ends with a malformed/missing verdict marker (the common first-after-restart case), the worker re-invokes run_claude under --resume with a terse correction up to this many times BEFORE writing the outbox, so the fix lands with zero cross-process marker-error round-trips. On exhaust the best-effort outbox is written and the existing outbox_notifier marker-error path stays as the outer backstop. Default 2; 0 disables the gate. Read by inbox_watcher._load_marker_self_validate_retries. See docs/tunables.md for retune triggers.

auto_merge_queue._note: D3.5 5d-prime serializer watchdog. When a PR sits in the auto-merge queue (held behind an overlapping in-flight PR) for longer than this, the notifier sweep DMs Larry once. Raise during planned multi-day absences so the queue doesn't spam him; lower during high-throughput periods. Read by outbox_notifier._load_auto_merge_watchdog_hours_from_config; cache invalidates on daemon restart.
auto_merge_queue._note_revalidate: fix-auto-merge-freshness-revalidation (2026-06-11). When a HELD auto-merge is released (its overlapping blocker merged, so main moved under the pre-hold approval), the release path re-validates against CURRENT main before merging: re-confirm mergeable, and — when the base actually moved since approval — re-run the regression gate (test_regression_check.py). A regressing/conflicting/unverifiable PR is NOT auto-merged; Larry is DMed to re-review/rebase. Motivated by the 2026-06-11 PR #455 incident (held ~6h, fired 11s after the blocker merged on a stale approval, landed a +13-test regression that mergeable=CLEAN didn't catch). revalidate_regression_on_release gates the (expensive) regression re-run — leave true; set false ONLY as an emergency escape hatch (the cheap mergeable re-confirm still runs). release_regression_timeout_per_sha_s bounds the inline test_regression_check.py shell-out per SHA so a hung suite can't wedge the notifier poll loop (holds are rare, so this fires infrequently); a timeout fails closed (the merge is held, not fired). Read by outbox_notifier._load_revalidate_regression_on_release_from_config / _load_release_regression_timeout_per_sha_s_from_config.

tier1_quota._note: DEPRECATED 2026-06-29 per Check VIII: the Tier-1 5h burn-rate token gate had ZERO predictive value — TP=0 across the trailing 8 weeks against 3,635 quota-events, with 4 false-positive DMs (precision 0.0, recall 0.0). Larry approved deprecation. Disabled via `enabled: false` (read by heal_claude_max_burn_rate.gate_enabled), NOT by deleting max_5h_token_threshold: load_threshold() fail-safes a missing/invalid threshold back to the 10M DEFAULT_MAX_5H_TOKEN_THRESHOLD + WARNs every tick, so deletion would keep the gate firing at exactly 10M and spam the log. The `enabled` flag governs; an ABSENT enabled key means enabled (back-compat — an accidentally-deleted field must not silently blind monitoring). max_5h_token_threshold is retained for historical provenance and because rotation (default-off) still reads it via load_threshold() for its engage/disengage fractions. When enabled=false a healer tick computes nothing and DMs nothing. HISTORICAL: rolling 5h quota-consuming token ceiling for the Tier 1 Claude Max account. heal_claude_max_burn_rate.py DMed Larry once when summed costs.jsonl input+output+cache_creation tokens in the trailing 5h window crossed 80% of this. Re-based 2026-05-28 from the prior $60 dollar threshold (max_5h_spend_threshold_usd) — we run OAuth Max with no per-token billing, so dollar sums were imputed-not-real and false-alarmed every ~15 min on 2026-05-27 while real Anthropic usage sat at 31% session / 59% weekly. The 10M seed sat above the 2026-05-27 false-alarm period's peak rolling-5h volume (~9.7M tokens) and below historical peak burn (~14M). cache_read was intentionally excluded — the largely-free cached re-read would inflate the signal 10-100x. V1 limitation: costs.jsonl has no per-account field so the sum included Tier 2 fallback usage (conservative — alerts slightly early).

rotation._note: Account-rotation scheduler config (spec § 6.3 + § 6.4 load gating). enabled is the master kill switch — flipping to false on the next tick forces tier1, clears draining, and disables both engage and drain-then-switch. tier1_window_minutes / tier2_window_minutes set the 2:1 ratio (120/60 = Tier 1 runs ~2/3 of the cycle). max_drain_minutes caps how long the scheduler waits for in-flight work to clear before deferring a flip (never force-kills). engage_at_fraction / disengage_at_fraction are the load-gate hysteresis thresholds expressed as fractions of tier1_quota.max_5h_token_threshold (the pulse-tuned Tier 1 quota ceiling read via heal_claude_max_burn_rate.load_threshold). Rotation ENGAGES when rolling_5h_token_volume >= engage_at_fraction * threshold; DISENGAGES (forces tier1 + clears drain) when usage < disengage_at_fraction * threshold; HOLDS current engaged state between the two so it does not flap near the boundary. Fractions track the pulse-tuned token threshold rather than a second hand-tuned constant — when Check VIII raises or lowers the threshold, the gate moves with it. tier1_home / tier2_home pin the two OAuth credential roots; must agree with scripts/active_tier.TIER1_HOME / TIER2_HOME. Master kill at any time: set enabled=false and the scheduler clears any partial drain state on the next 2-min tick. RETIRING: superseded by the per-task tier_pool below (spec docs/specs/tier-dispatch-spec.md). At cutover enabled flips to false and the rotation.disabled=tier2 pin is removed; the time-sliced rotation is replaced by round-robin dispatch across the primary pool.

tier_pool._note: Per-task tier-dispatch capacity pool (spec docs/specs/tier-dispatch-spec.md). Read by scripts/active_tier.select_dispatch_tier with fail-safe defaults (a missing/malformed block degrades to primary=[tier1], no proactive near_cap — never a crash). primary = round-robin pool of dedicated Max accounts {tier1, tier3}; fallback = tier2 (the laptop's personal account), emergency-only when BOTH primaries are benched and only under the reserve guard. proactive_cap_fraction / proactive_release_fraction = the near_cap hysteresis band as fractions of max_5h_budget_tokens (skip a primary at/above 0.85 of budget; re-include below 0.70). t2_reserve_fraction = 0.25 bounds the SYSTEM's OWN tier2 5h burn before an emergency spill holds (never drain Larry's laptop out from under him). max_5h_budget_tokens = the conservative bootstrap 5h token ceiling (~the documented 9.7M observed peak); § 12b self-tuning calibration OVERRIDES this PER TIER at runtime via ~/agents/state/tier-budget-calibration.json (no deploy). hold_alert_minutes = how long an all-tiers-held NEW dispatch waits before the deduped tier-pool-all-unavailable alert fires (§ 9). Decisions LOCKED 2026-06-30: v1 round-robin (burn-weighted = v2); 25% T2 reserve; self-tuning calibration required.

haiku._note: Used by heal_tier2_weekly_health_probe.py for cheap liveness probes against the Tier 2 OAuth account. Cheapest viable model — probe is intentionally minimal (~$0.001 per run). Pin the latest Haiku id here; the healer falls back to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 if this block is missing.

check_x_regression._note: Pulse Check X (scripts/pulse_check_x.py) — weekly chain-quality regression watch over the Forge/Mirror auto-merge chain. Read-only analyzer; NEVER edits this file. Compares a trailing window (most recent window_days) against a baseline window (window_days immediately before cutover_date) and DMs Larry only when a regression is suspected — he reviews + disposes (no auto-action). cutover_date is the model/prompt change being watched (default 2026-06-01, the Opus 4.8 Forge/Mirror roll-forward); re-point it for any future change. min_tasks_per_window is the anti-cry-wolf floor: below it in EITHER window the cycle logs insufficient_signal and stays silent (Forge/Mirror volume is modest); it also gates the verdict-mix thresholds (a window with fewer than this many Mirror verdicts is treated as insufficient verdict history). ALL FOUR thresholds are now ACTIVE. clarify_rate_rel_increase and revision_rounds_rel_increase are relative-increase detectors (trailing vs baseline): clarify_rate_rel_increase is applied to clarify-ROUNDS-per-task (clarify_request chain_events / distinct Forge task), and revision_rounds_rel_increase to a costs.jsonl proxy (Forge build-work dispatches beyond the first, per task_id). escalate_rate_abs_increase and pass_rate_abs_drop are absolute-change detectors on the Mirror verdict mix (review_pass/review_revision/review_escalate chain_events, push-emitted by outbox_notifier as of the check-x-verdict-emission PR): escalate_rate = escalates/total, pass_rate = passes/total per window. HONEST LIMITATION: verdict emission started at that PR's merge, so the 4.8 baseline (before 2026-06-01) has NO verdict events — the verdict-mix thresholds sit at insufficient_signal for 4.8 and activate only for FUTURE cutovers once verdict history exists on both sides of cutover_date; the clarify/revision thresholds remain the 4.8 read. All four are additive defaults — tune as data accrues.
